speaker_title: Address by Mr. Imran Khan, Prime Minister of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: I congratulate you on assuming the presidency of the 76th session of the General Assembly.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I congratulate you on assuming the presidency of the 76th session of the 
General Assembly.

paragraphs.text: I also wish to express appreciation for the significant achievements of your predecessor, Volkan Bozkır, who guided the Assembly skilfully under the difficult circumstances imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I also wish to express appreciation for the significant achievements of your 
predecessor, Volkan Bozkır, who guided the Assembly skilfully under the difficult 
circumstances imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: The world is facing triple challenge of the COVID-19, the accompanying economic crisis, and the threats posed by climate change.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The world is facing triple challenge of the COVID-19, the accompanying 
economic crisis, and the threats posed by climate change.

paragraphs.text: The virus does not discriminate between nations and people. Nor do the catastrophes imposed by uncertain weather patterns.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The virus does not discriminate between nations and people. Nor do the 
catastrophes imposed by uncertain weather patterns.

paragraphs.text: The common threats faced by us today not only expose the fragility of the international system; they also underscore the oneness of humanity.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The common threats faced by us today not only expose the fragility of the 
international system; they also underscore the oneness of humanity.

paragraphs.text: By the grace of Almighty Allah, Pakistan has been successful so far in containing the COVID pandemic. Our calibrated strategy of ‘smart lockdowns’ helped save lives and livelihoods and kept the economy afloat. Over 15 million families survived through our social protection programme of Ehsaas.
paragraphs.raw_text:
By the grace of Almighty Allah, Pakistan has been successful so far in 
containing the COVID pandemic. Our calibrated strategy of ‘smart lockdowns’ 
helped save lives and livelihoods and kept the economy afloat. Over 15 million 
families survived through our social protection programme of Ehsaas.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Climate change is one of the primary existential threats that our planet faces today.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Climate change is one of the primary existential threats that our planet 
faces today.

paragraphs.text: Pakistan’s contribution to global emissions is negligible. Yet we are among the 10 most vulnerable countries to the effects of climate change in the world.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Pakistan’s contribution to global emissions is negligible. Yet we are among the 
10 most vulnerable countries to the effects of climate change in the world.

paragraphs.text: Being fully aware of our global responsibilities, we have embarked upon gamechanging environmental programmes: reforesting Pakistan through our 10 billion tree tsunami; preserving natural habitats; switching to renewable energy; removing pollution from our cities; and adapting to the impacts of climate change.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Being fully aware of our global responsibilities, we have embarked upon game-
changing environmental programmes: reforesting Pakistan through our 10 billion 
tree tsunami; preserving natural habitats; switching to renewable energy; removing 
pollution from our cities; and adapting to the impacts of climate change.

paragraphs.text: To address the triple crisis of COVID pandemic, economic downturn, and climate emergency, we need a comprehensive strategy that should include:
paragraphs.raw_text:
To address the triple crisis of COVID pandemic, economic downturn, and 
climate emergency, we need a comprehensive strategy that should include:

paragraphs.text: One, vaccine equity: everyone, everywhere, must be vaccinated against COVID, and as soon as possible;
paragraphs.raw_text:
One, vaccine equity: everyone, everywhere, must be vaccinated against 
COVID, and as soon as possible;

paragraphs.text: Two, adequate financing must be made available to developing countries. This can be ensured through comprehensive debt restructuring; expanded ODA; redistribution of unutilized SDRs, and allotment of a greater proportion of SDRs to developing countries; and finally, provision of climate finance; and
paragraphs.raw_text:
Two, adequate financing must be made available to developing countries. 
This can be ensured through comprehensive debt restructuring; expanded ODA; 
redistribution of unutilized SDRs, and allotment of a greater proportion of SDRs to 
developing countries; and finally, provision of climate finance; and

paragraphs.text: Three, we must adopt clear investment strategies which help alleviate poverty, promote job creation, build sustainable infrastructure, and of course bridge the digital divide.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Three, we must adopt clear investment strategies which help alleviate poverty, 
promote job creation, build sustainable infrastructure, and of course bridge the 
digital divide.

paragraphs.text: I propose that the Secretary-General convene an SDG summit in 2025 to review and accelerate implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
paragraphs.raw_text:
I propose that the Secretary-General convene an SDG summit in 2025 to 
review and accelerate implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Because of the plunder of the developing world by their corrupt ruling elites, the gap between the rich and the poor countries is increasing at an alarming speed.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Because of the plunder of the developing world by their corrupt ruling elites, 
the gap between the rich and the poor countries is increasing at an alarming speed.

paragraphs.text: Through this platform, I have been drawing the world’s attention towards the scourge of illicit financial flows from developing countries.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Through this platform, I have been drawing the world’s attention towards the 
scourge of illicit financial flows from developing countries.

paragraphs.text: The Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Financial Accountability, Transparency and Integrity (FACTI) has calculated that a staggering $7 trillion in stolen assets are parked in the financial “haven” destinations.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The Secretary-General’s High-Level Panel on Financial Accountability, 
Transparency and Integrity (FACTI) has calculated that a staggering $7 trillion in 
stolen assets are parked in the financial “haven” destinations.

paragraphs.text: This organized theft and illegal transfer of assets has profound consequences for the developing nations. It depletes their already meagre resources, accentuates the levels of poverty especially when laundered money puts pressure on the currency and leads to its devaluation. At the current rate, when the FACTI Panel estimates that a trillion dollars every year are taken out of the developing world, there will be mass exodus of economic migrants towards the richer nations.
paragraphs.raw_text:
This organized theft and illegal transfer of assets has profound consequences 
for the developing nations. It depletes their already meagre resources, accentuates 
the levels of poverty especially when laundered money puts pressure on the currency 
and leads to its devaluation. At the current rate, when the FACTI Panel estimates that 
a trillion dollars every year are taken out of the developing world, there will be mass 
exodus of economic migrants towards the richer nations.

paragraphs.text: What the East India Company did to India, the crooked ruling elites are doing to developing world — plundering the wealth and transferring to western capitals and offshore tax havens.
paragraphs.raw_text:
What the East India Company did to India, the crooked ruling elites are doing 
to developing world — plundering the wealth and transferring to western capitals and 
offshore tax havens.

paragraphs.text: And Mr. President, retrieving the stolen assets from the developed countries is impossible for poor nations. The rich countries have no incentives, or compulsion, to return this ill-gotten wealth, and this ill-gotten wealth belongs to the masses of the developing world. I foresee, in the not-too-distant future a time will come when the rich countries will be forced to build walls to keep out economic migrants from these poor countries.
paragraphs.raw_text:
And Mr. President, retrieving the stolen assets from the developed countries 
is impossible for poor nations. The rich countries have no incentives, or compulsion, 
to return this ill-gotten wealth, and this ill-gotten wealth belongs to the masses of 
the developing world. I foresee, in the not-too-distant future a time will come when

paragraphs.text: I fear a few “wealthy islands” in the sea of poverty will also turn into a global calamity, like climate change.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I fear a few “wealthy islands” in the sea of poverty will also turn into a global 
calamity, like climate change.

paragraphs.text: The General Assembly must take steps meaningfully to address this deeply disturbing, and morally repugnant, situation. Naming and shaming the ‘haven’ destinations and developing a comprehensive legal framework to halt and reverse the illicit financial flows are most critical actions to stop this grave economic injustice.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The General Assembly must take steps meaningfully to address this deeply 
disturbing, and morally repugnant, situation. Naming and shaming the ‘haven’ 
destinations and developing a comprehensive legal framework to halt and reverse the 
illicit financial flows are most critical actions to stop this grave economic injustice.

paragraphs.text: And at a minimum, the recommendations of Secretary-General’s FACTI panel should be fully implemented.
paragraphs.raw_text:
And at a minimum, the recommendations of Secretary-General’s FACTI panel 
should be fully implemented.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Islamophobia is another pernicious phenomenon that we all need to collectively combat.
paragraphs.raw_text:
Islamophobia is another pernicious phenomenon that we all need to 
collectively combat.

paragraphs.text: In the aftermath of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, terrorism has been associated with Islam by some quarters. This has increased the tendency of right-wing, xenophobic and violent nationalists, extremists and terrorist groups to target Muslims.
paragraphs.raw_text:
In the aftermath of the 9/11 terrorist attacks, terrorism has been associated with 
Islam by some quarters. This has increased the tendency of right-wing, xenophobic 
and violent nationalists, extremists and terrorist groups to target Muslims.

paragraphs.text: The UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy has recognized these emerging threats. We hope the Secretary-General’s report will focus on these new threats of terrorism posed by Islamophobes and right-wing extremists.
paragraphs.raw_text:
The UN Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy has recognized these emerging 
threats. We hope the Secretary-General’s report will focus on these new threats of 
terrorism posed by Islamophobes and right-wing extremists.

paragraphs.text: I call on the Secretary-General to convene a global dialogue on countering the rise of Islamophobia. Our parallel efforts, at the same time, should be to promote interfaith harmony, and they should continue.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I call on the Secretary-General to convene a global dialogue on countering 
the rise of Islamophobia. Our parallel efforts, at the same time, should be to promote 
interfaith harmony, and they should continue.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: The worst and most pervasive form of Islamophobia now rules India. The hatefilled Hindutva ideology, propagated by the fascist RSS-BJP regime, has unleashed a reign of fear and violence against India’s 200 million strong Muslim community. Mob lynching by cow vigilantes; frequent pogroms, such as the one in New Delhi last year; discriminatory citizenship laws to purge India of Muslims; and a campaign to destroy mosques across India and obliterate its Muslim heritage and history, are all part of this criminal enterprise.

paragraphs.text: This repression is accompanied by illegal efforts to change the demographic structure of the occupied territory, and transform it from a Muslim majority into a Muslim minority.
paragraphs.raw_text:

paragraphs.text: Indian actions violate the resolutions of the UN Security Council on Jammu and Kashmir. The resolutions clearly prescribe that the “final disposition” of the disputed territory should be decided by its people, through a free and impartial plebiscite held under the UN auspices.

paragraphs.raw_text:

Geopolitical considerations, or corporate interests, commercial interests often compel major powers to overlook the transgressions of their “affiliated” countries.

paragraphs.text: Such double standards are the most glaring in case of India, where this RSS-BJP regime is being allowed to get away with human rights abuses with complete impunity.

paragraphs.text: The most recent example of Indian barbarity was the forcible snatching of the mortal remains of the great Kashmiri leader, Syed Ali Shah Geelani, from his family, denying him a proper Islamic funeral and burial, in accordance with his wishes and Muslim traditions.
paragraphs.raw_text:

mortal remains of the great Kashmiri leader, Syed Ali Shah Geelani, from his family, 
denying him a proper Islamic funeral and burial, in accordance with his wishes and 
Muslim traditions.

paragraphs.text: Devoid of any legal or moral sanction, this action was even against the basic norms of human decency. I call on this General Assembly to demand that Syed Geelani’s mortal remains be allowed to be buried in the “cemetery of martyrs” with the appropriate Islamic rites.

paragraphs.text: Mr. President,
paragraphs.raw_text: Mr. President,

paragraphs.text: Pakistan desires peace with India, as with all its neighbours. But sustainable peace in South Asia is contingent upon resolution of the Jammu and Kashmir dispute, in accordance with the relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions, and the wishes of the Kashmiri people.

paragraphs.text: And now Mr. President, I want to talk about Afghanistan. For the current situation in Afghanistan, for some reason, Pakistan has been blamed for the turn of events, by politicians in the United States and some politicians in Europe.
paragraphs.raw_text:
And now Mr. President, I want to talk about Afghanistan. For the current 
situation in Afghanistan, for some reason, Pakistan has been blamed for the turn of 
events, by politicians in the United States and some politicians in Europe.

paragraphs.text: From this platform, I want them all to know, the country that suffered the most, apart from Afghanistan, was Pakistan, when we joined the US War on Terror after 9/11.
paragraphs.raw_text:
From this platform, I want them all to know, the country that suffered the 
most, apart from Afghanistan, was Pakistan, when we joined the US War on Terror

paragraphs.text: Some 80,000 Pakistanis died. $150 billion dollars were lost to our economy. There were 3.5 million internally displaced Pakistanis. And why did this happen? In the 1980s, Pakistan was a front-line state in fighting against the occupation of Afghanistan. Pakistan and the United States trained Mujahideen groups to fight for the liberation of Afghanistan. Amongst those Mujahideen groups was Al-Qaeda, various groups from all over the world. There were Mujahideen, Afghan Mujahideen. These were considered heroes.

paragraphs.text: Come 1989, the Soviets leave, and so do the Americans — abandoning Afghanistan. Pakistan was left with 5 million Afghan refugees. We were left with sectarian militant groups which were never existed before. But the worse cut of it was, that a year later Pakistan was sanctioned by the US. We felt used.

paragraphs.text: Fast forward 9/11, Pakistan is needed again by the US, because now the US- led coalition was invading Afghanistan, and it could not happen without Pakistan providing all the logistical support.
paragraphs.raw_text:

paragraphs.text: What happened after that?
paragraphs.raw_text: What happened after that?

paragraphs.text: The same Mujahideen that we had trained, that fighting foreign occupation was a sacred duty, a holy war or jehad, turned against us.
paragraphs.raw_text:

paragraphs.text: We were called collaborators.
paragraphs.raw_text: We were called collaborators.

paragraphs.text: They declared jihad on us. Then all along the tribal belt bordering Afghanistan — Pakistan’s semi-autonomous tribal belt — where no Pakistan army had been there since our independence, people had strong sympathies with the Afghan Taliban, not because of their religious ideology but because of Pashtun nationalism, which is very strong. Then there are three million Afghan refugees still in Pakistan all Pashtuns, living in the camps. 500,000 in the biggest camp, 100,000 camps. They all had affinity and sympathy with the Afghan Taliban.

There is a huge humanitarian crisis looming ahead. And this will have serious repercussions not just for the neighbours of Afghanistan but everywhere. A destabilized, chaotic Afghanistan will again become a safe haven for international terrorists — the reason why the US came to Afghanistan in the first place.

paragraphs.text: If the world community incentivizes them, and encourages them to walk this talk, it will be a win-win situation for everyone. Because these are the four conditions that the US-Taliban dialogue in Doha was all about.

If the world community incentivizes them, and encourages them to walk this 
talk, it will be a win-win situation for everyone. Because these are the four conditions 
that the US-Taliban dialogue in Doha was all about.

paragraphs.text: If the world can incentivise them to go this direction, then this twenty-year presence of the coalition forces in Afghanistan would not be wasted after all. Because the Afghan soil would not be used by the international terrorists.
paragraphs.raw_text:

paragraphs.text: I end Mr. President, by urging everyone that this is a critical time for Afghanistan.
paragraphs.raw_text:
I end Mr. President, by urging everyone that this is a critical time for 
Afghanistan.

paragraphs.text: You cannot waste time. Help is needed there. Humanitarian assistance has to be given there immediately. The Secretary General of the United Nations has taken bold steps. I urge you to mobilize the international community, and move in this direction.

paragraphs.text: Thank you.
